brief:
Residents across Gaza are preparing for another winter of severe cold and rain without adequate shelter, as families endure life in damaged buildings and deteriorating tents, UN News reported. Ahmed Al-Omari is among those facing the season with minimal protection against flooding and freezing temperatures.

The strip's war-damaged infrastructure leaves residents vulnerable to the elements. Families are improvising defenses—including using flour sacks as flood barriers—to protect themselves from winter weather in a territory where safe housing remains scarce.
dek: Like many people in the war-ravaged Gaza Strip, Ahmed Al-Omari is preparing for another winter of bitter cold and rain that threatens to cause flooding as families struggle to survive in tattered tents and damaged buildings.
title: Gazans brace for winter without shelter as flooding threats mount
